title: A trip-started message arrives after an identification for that trip was already written
description: Trip-start consumer case. The identification is delivered live at deliverAtSec 0, claiming atSec 10. The trip's own frames (IGN_ON at atSec 0, so its start_date precedes the identification's claimed timestamp) are sent as a full burst starting at burstStartAtSec 5, i.e. the trip-started message is delivered 5 seconds AFTER the identification, even though the trip's own start_date is earlier. The trip is deliberately left open (no IGN_OFF): this case tests only the trip-start consumer's ordering, not trip close. Must prove: the trip-start consumer links the row, awards the claim, and writes both assignees as soon as the trip-started message arrives, even though it arrived after the identification. Must NOT change: before the trip-started message arrives, the identification must sit unlinked with no assignee written anywhere.

events.note: trip-started message delivered after the identification, backdated to start before it; trip deliberately left open

driver_identifications.note: identification for a trip that has not started yet, from Tenna's perspective
